body: Pushmo is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS puzzle game about rescuing children trapped in large structures made from sliding blocks. Known as Pullblox in Europe, it stars Mallo, a small red character who can push and pull sections of a colourful design to make a climbable route. A picture that first looks flat becomes a set of platforms with different depths. The goal is visible, but reaching it requires changing the structure beneath it. The puzzle is both an image to understand and a space that must support Mallo's next jump.

Pulling one block creates a ledge, but the position of neighbouring pieces determines whether that ledge can actually be reached. Mallo must stand in the right place to manipulate a section, so a solution includes the route taken while constructing it. The player learns to consider depth as well as height. A promising arrangement can leave no room for the next action, requiring another approach. The tactile rhythm of pull, climb and inspect makes a compact set of movements capable of supporting increasingly elaborate spatial problems.

Pushmo Park supplies a friendly setting for these structures, with Papa Blox introducing the play area and the trapped children providing a clear destination. The characters make the objective understandable before the arrangement becomes complicated. Each rescue is a complete little journey from the ground to the point inside the design where somebody is waiting. The stereoscopic display suits that journey by making the separate depths easy to inspect. Pushmo finds personality in a practical act: reshaping a playful object until another person can be reached.
